chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, who said:
I heard Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام say regarding a man who sought to induce a woman to commit something unlawful against herself,
and she threw a stone at him, striking a fatal spot. He عليه السلام said: “There is nothing upon her in what is between her and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”
And if she is brought before a just Imam, he will deem his blood without liability.

key_terms.أَهْدَرَ دَمَهُ: declared his blood without liability or compensation
key_terms.إِمَامٍ عَدْلٍ: a just Imam with lawful judicial authority
key_terms.بِحَجَرٍ: with a stone; the object used in self-defense
key_terms.مَقْتَلًا: a fatal spot or mortal blow

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman kills a man while defending herself from unlawful sexual assault?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a woman who kills a man while defending herself from an unlawful sexual assault. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that she bears no blame before Allah عزّ وجلّ, and that under the judgment of a just Imam, the assailant’s blood is treated as without compensable liability.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5373 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah (as) say regarding a man who tried to seduce a woman for unlawful relations, and she threw a stone at him, striking him in a fatal spot and killing him.
Imam (as) said: "There is nothing upon her in the matter between her and Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic.
And if she is brought before a just Imam, he will declare his blood to be void."
